questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate option.

So, I __________ out my 10 thousand dollars and I said, 'If I didn't get it, I'd start a bank by myself.'
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**stuck**" is the correct past tense of "stick" when used in this context. (अटका)
 
• Example: He **stuck **out his hand to greet the new employee.
 
• In the context, "So, I **stuck** out my 10 thousand dollars and I said, 'If I didn't get it, I'd start a bank by myself.'" means that the speaker confidently showed or offered the money.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**stuck**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *So, I **stuck **out my 10 thousand dollars and I said, 'If I didn't get it, I'd start a bank by myself.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stucked (Not a standard word, incorrect usage in any context)**
 
• **Stick (चिपकाना/लाठी)**: Present tense of "stick," not appropriate in past tense context.
 
• **Sticked (Not a standard word, incorrect usage in any context)**

They __often drinks__ wine with their meals.

• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect verb form "**drinks**" which does not agree with the plural subject "**They**."
 
• In English, the verb must agree with the subject in number; here, the correct form should be "**drink**."
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be "**They often drink wine with their meals**," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They** often drink **wine with their meals."*

• The phrase **"than she had been when"** is grammatically correct and appropriately conveys the intended meaning.
 
• None of the other options provide a grammatically correct or meaningful alternative.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She was even more dreadfully fond of Estella **than she had been when** I last saw them together."*

• **Example: **The probate process ensures that the deceased's assets are distributed according to their will.
 
 
 
• **Permit (अनुमति देना)**: To allow something to happen, give authorization.
 
 
• **Example: **The authorities permit fishing in this area only during certain months.
 
 
 
• **Peruse (ध्यानपूर्वक पढ़ना)**: To read or examine something with great care.
 
 
• **Example: **Please peruse the document before signing.

• The word "**for**" indicates the purpose of something. (के लिए)
 
• Example: He is looking** for** his keys.
 
• In the context, "Residential and commercial buildings use electricity for air-conditioning and lighting and oil and natural gas **for** heating" means that these buildings use oil and natural gas with the purpose of heating.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**for**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Coal and natural gas-fired power plants generate electricity. Oil-based products such as gasoline, diesel fuel, and aviation fuel provide most of the energy used in transportation. The industry also uses fossil fuels to produce power and heat needed by industrial processes. Residential and commercial buildings use electricity for air-conditioning and lighting and oil and natural gas **for**__ heating.*

• **In (में)**: Indicates the location or position within something.

 
 
• **Example: **The book is in the bag.
 
 
 
• **Of (का)**: Indicates belonging or relating to something.
 
 
• **Example: **The leg of the table is broken.
 
 
 
• **To (तक)**: Used to indicate direction or movement toward a place, thing, or part.
 
 
• **Example: **I am going to the market.
